Dcode

The coding agent for air-gapped teams and local LLMs — built for open-source models with small context windows.

v0.6.0Terminal · Web UI · EditorsAny OpenAI-compatible serverTested on vLLM100% offline
The problem

AI coding tools assume the cloud.
Many teams can't use the cloud.

🔒

Code can't leave

Banks, government, defense, telecom and regulated industries run on air-gapped or restricted networks. Source code must stay inside.

🧠

Local models are small

Self-hosted 7B–32B models usually have 8K–32K of context — a fraction of what cloud agents are designed for.

🧩

And they're sloppy

Open models write tool calls as text, leak markup, stop mid-task, announce work they never do, and loop. Agents built for frontier models fall apart.

Dcode is built from the ground up for exactly this environment.

Meet Dcode

One binary. Your models. Your network.

Ask in plain language — "fix the failing test", "why does this deploy crash?", "explain this repo". Dcode reads your code, edits files, runs commands, queries databases and checks git, showing every step and asking before anything risky.

⌨️

Terminal agent

Keyboard-first CLI with modes, approvals and a live activity panel.

🖥️

Web UI

A private localhost UI per user, driving the same live sessions.

🧠

Several models

A main model, a stronger one for hard tasks, a small one for side jobs — each on its own server.

📦

Air-gap ready

One self-contained binary as .deb, .rpm, tarball or Docker image. No internet, no pip.

Also: databases, scheduled jobs, local MCP tools, VS Code and Zed, and dcode attach from another terminal.

First run on real local models

vLLM on a GPU cluster, 16K context

Main: gemma4:31b · Reasoning: diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it, each its own vLLM deployment. A small project with two real bugs: a lock taken twice, and a KeyError.

TestWhat happened
Easy questionStayed on the main model · 7 s
"Why does reserve() hang? Find the root cause and fix it"Routed to the reasoning model · found the double lock, fixed both bugs · 3/3 tests pass · 12–15 s
Six-turn chatMoved between both models with the history intact
Plan modeStayed on the main model
Helpers set to the reasoning modelRan there, on its own server

🐞 Found and fixed

Models copied the space after N| as indentation, so edits failed; a model ignored the repeat warning and looped. Both fixed, with regression tests.

⏱ Measured

About 7 tokens/s (gemma4) vs. 240 (diffusiongemma) on that cluster: the servers, not Dcode, set the pace.

Built for small context windows

Every token of a 32K window counts

  • Read only what's needed — numbered line ranges, regex search, depth-limited listing.
  • Edit, don't rewrite — exact-match edit_file instead of re-sending whole files.
  • Output caps scale with the window — about 12% per tool result; long command output keeps head and tail.
  • Helpers explore elsewhere — only a short report returns to the main conversation.
  • Index, don't inline — skills, memories and MCP tools appear as names; details load on demand.
  • Automatic compaction at ~75%: trim old tool output first, then summarize older turns.

Robust with real open models

Small models make mistakes. Dcode absorbs them.

🔁 Follow-through

"Building the artifact now." — and it stops? Dcode reminds the model to actually do it (capped, never loops).

🧾 Text tool calls

Recovers calls written as <tool_call> or fenced JSON when the server doesn't parse them.

🧹 Leaked markup

Cleans tags models leak into tool names (e.g. DeepSeek ｜DSML｜) and salvages arguments.

✏️ Forgiving edits

Accepts pasted line numbers and blocks copied one space too deep; a failed edit names the line it probably meant.

✂️ Cut-off replies

Hits the output limit? Dcode asks it to continue; big artifacts can be built in parts.

🛡️ Guard rails

Refuses empty writes that would erase a file; stops a model stuck repeating one call; nudges silent stops.

Reasoning (<think> or the server's own field) is shown on request with /thinking and never refills the context. Dcode also learns which optional parameters a server rejects.

Multi-agent

Helpers do the legwork — in their own context

🧭 Explorer

Finds and reads code; reports facts with file:line references. Read-only.

💻 Coder

Makes one well-defined change with minimal edits.

👁 Reviewer

Reviews code or a diff for real bugs and security issues. Read-only.

🧪 Tester

Writes and runs focused tests; reports pass/fail.

  • Read-only helpers run in parallel; only a capped report comes back
  • Your own helpers in .dcode/agents/*.md · call one with @name
  • Each can run on its own model — even another server
  • Open a helper's own session in the web UI: every step it took
You stay in control

Four modes — Shift+Tab to switch

Accept edits

Default. Edits files freely; asks before commands, deletions and commits.

Auto

Never asks. For trusted, sandboxed projects only.

Plan

Read-only. Investigates and writes a plan, then asks "Ready to implement this plan?"

Manual

Asks before every edit (with a diff preview) and every command.

Approvals, your way

Allow · Allow for this session · Deny — from the terminal menu (y a n) or a card in the web UI. Whichever answers first wins; the menu then shrinks to a single line.

Undo anything Dcode changed

Every task saves a checkpoint. /undo restores the files — even outside git — and /redo brings them back. The model is told either way.

The terminal

Keyboard-first, calm, and informative

  • Input pinned to the bottom; white text, blue only for structure
  • @file attaches a file · !command runs your own shell command
  • /thinking · /details · /notify · /editor for long messages
  • /sessions, dcode --continue · /export md · html · json
  • Every task ends with a report; inline diffs for edits
  • Ctrl+O expands output · Ctrl+C stops · twice exits
The web UI

A private, ChatGPT-style UI for every user

  • Live sessions and past chats; export or import a chat

Memory & skills

It remembers your project — and follows your playbooks

🧠 Three layers of memory

Working — the live chat, compacted. Episodic — summaries of past sessions. Semantic — saved facts per project or global. Plain Markdown, searched offline (BM25), recalled automatically.

⚡ Skills

Nine built in: devops, developer, ui-designer, code-reviewer, artifact-creator, tester, security-auditor, docs-writer, debugger. Dcode picks the right one; pin favorites. Create your own by asking Dcode, in the UI, or with a .md file — shareable per project via git.

Works the way your project does

Checks its own edits, follows your conventions

✅ Checks after every edit

Python, JSON, TOML, shell, JS, Go and more — plus your own commands. Errors go straight back to the model.

📎 @file mentions

Fuzzy completion; the file is attached as if the model had read it — no tool call spent.

☑️ A checklist

Multi-step work gets a visible checklist that the model keeps up to date.

📄 /init

Writes AGENTS.md: build and test commands, layout and conventions, read on every task.

❓ Questions

When something is unclear, Dcode asks you with a short menu instead of guessing.

⚡ Your commands

.dcode/commands/*.md become slash commands, with arguments and shell snippets.

Databases

Look at your data like an admin would

  • PostgreSQL, MySQL / MariaDB and SQLite — drivers bundled
  • Schema, data, a summary, and exports with size guards
  • Reads run in a read-only session with a timeout
  • Every change asks first — in every mode, never "for the session"
  • The model can query too: db_schema, db_query
  • Web UI or /db; passwords are never sent back
Scheduled jobs

Cron jobs with logs — commands or Dcode tasks

  • Standard cron expressions, read back in plain words
  • A shell command, or a prompt for dcode run
  • Every run's output kept, with exit code and time limit
  • Unattended runs deny approvals: the job's mode says what it may do
  • No cron daemon needed · /cron or the Scheduled screen
Extend it

Your tools, your rules

A local MCP server: ready, 6 tools

🔌 MCP servers

Local programs give Dcode extra tools. Only their names enter the prompt — 46 tools cost under 400 characters. Every call asks unless you allow it.

🚦 Rules

Allow, ask or deny commands and files by pattern. .env is denied by default; projects can only tighten.

🪝 Hooks

Your shell commands before or after tools, when a task ends, or when Dcode needs you.

Everyday workflow

Git-aware, and honest about what it did

/diff · /commit

See uncommitted changes in color; commit with a message Dcode writes from the diff — after you confirm.

/undo · /redo

Roll back the files Dcode changed in the last task, git or not — and bring them back.

/compact

Summarize a long session into a short memory and free the context window.

⚙ Background jobs

Servers and watchers run in the background; /jobs shows output or stops them.

📋 Task reports

Every task ends with what changed, which commands ran, and what's left.

🏷️ Named chats

Titled from your first message; /sessions, --continue or the web UI bring them back.

Safe by default

An agent that runs model output needs guard rails

📁 Workspace sandbox

File tools stay in the project; paths outside it ask first.

✋ Approvals

Commands, deletions and commits ask; empty writes that would erase a file are refused.

🚦 Rules

Allow · ask · deny by pattern. .env denied by default; projects can only tighten.

🗄️ Database changes

Reads are read-only sessions. Every change asks — even in auto mode.

🔌 External tools

MCP servers and hooks come only from your own config, never from a project.

🔑 Private web UI

127.0.0.1 only, per-user token, CSRF and DNS-rebinding protection.

🧱 Sandboxed artifacts

Isolated iframes with no network (CSP default-src 'none').

🗝️ Secrets

~/.dcode is owner-only; API keys and passwords are never sent back to the UI.

↩️ Reversible

Checkpoints for every task; nothing is pushed or committed without you.

Deploy

From build machine to air-gapped server in four steps

Build

One portable binary (glibc 2.28) and every package:

make packages

Copy

USB or internal mirror — one package, plus the installer:

.deb · .rpm · .tar.gz
or a Docker image
install-airgap.sh

Install

No internet, no pip:

sudo ./install-airgap.sh \
  dcode_0.6.0_amd64.deb

Point & run

At your local model:

export DCODE_BASE_URL=\
  http://gpu:8000/v1
export DCODE_MODEL=\
  qwen2.5-coder
dcode

Runs on RHEL 8+, Debian 10+ and Ubuntu 20.04+. Configuration lives in ~/.dcode/config.json or environment variables (env wins — handy for shared servers).

1.0

1.0 · stable

Frozen config and commands, fixes from validation, then the stable release.

Honest status: a well-tested beta. It now works with real local models on vLLM, and that first run already found two bugs. Not yet proven on a fully offline machine, on other servers, or in long sessions — that is what 1.0 will prove.
